annotations.banked_text_verbatim: BOUNDED AWAY FROM ZERO and truncation-independent.  The N=1024 row rises instead of falling -- that is the float floor of an X Gram whose entries reach ~1e12, not a mathematical statement, and it is why the reliable window stops at 512.  This is float64 EVIDENCE of a positive limit, not a proof of one: a decreasing positive sequence is reported as what it is.
annotations.what_is_wrong_with_it: The field OPENS with 'BOUNDED AWAY FROM ZERO and truncation-independent' -- an unqualified two-part claim -- and only its LAST sentence supplies the hedge ('float64 EVIDENCE of a positive limit, not a proof of one').  A reader or a later document quoting the field's opening phrase alone carries away two assertions the repository's own data do not support at the precision the numbers are quoted to.

verdict_on_each_half.bounded away from zero: SUPPORTED ONLY AS FLOAT64 EVIDENCE, not as a proof.  The field's own last sentence says so.  No proved floor on sigma_min is established anywhere in leg 176 or in PUB2; TECHNICAL_P2_PUB2_V1.md section 3.5 states that limitation in full.
verdict_on_each_half.truncation-independent: FALSE at the precision the ladder is quoted to.  The sigma_min ladder over the reliable window [32, 64, 128, 256, 512] varies by relative_spread = 0.0013899483438452888, i.e. 0.139 % over a 16-fold truncation range -- flat, measurably, but not independent.  The companion descriptor correction for the TAIL block is leg 268's K3; this entry is its C1 counterpart.

annotations.corrected_framing_to_quote_instead: sigma_min is FLAT across the reliable window -- 0.0908, varying by 0.139 % over a 16-fold truncation range (N = 32 ... 512) -- which is float64 EVIDENCE of a positive limit and not a proof of one.  No proved floor is claimed.
annotations.banked_values_this_annotation_changes: NONE.  ladder, reliable_window, sigma_min_at_512, resolvent_norm_at_512, spread_over_reliable_window, relative_spread, monotone_decreasing_through_512 and n1024_breaks_monotonicity are all left exactly as banked, and this file asserts nothing about any of them beyond leg 268's already-recorded K1 correction to sigma_min_at_512's 7th significant figure onward.
annotations.also_note: Leg 268's K1 established that leg 176's eigh whitening, not the X Gram's float floor, is what makes the N = 1024 row rise; under a Cholesky whitening the ladder is monotone decreasing through N = 2048.  So the reading field's stated CAUSE for the N=1024 rise is also superseded -- by leg 268/249, not by this leg -- and the reliable window is WIDER than leg 176 claimed, not narrower.
